$comment: Cross-language contract guard (issue #204). The SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for
which CommandErrorCode the Worker's instancemanager emits per command kind and
instance precondition. Rows mirror
worker/internal/application/instancemanager/instancemanager.go. 'kind' is the
Worker command kind (Handle's switch); 'code' is the wire CommandErrorCode name
(CONTROL_PLANE.md Section 7), 'ok' a success.
THE RULE (issue #2472): this table is EXHAUSTIVE OVER WORKER EMISSIONS, not over
API match sites. Concretely:
1. 'kinds' is every kind Manager.Handle dispatches and 'preconditions' every
Worker state the rows key on. 'rows' is the FULL MATRIX of the two: exactly
one row per (kind, precondition) cell, none missing, none twice.
2. A cell whose precondition determines no emission for that kind carries the
code 'unaffected' plus a 'why' saying HOW WE KNOW -- the handler takes no
instance check, the kind carries no path, it never invokes driver.Start. An
absent cell therefore always means FORGOTTEN, never 'not applicable'. That
distinction is the whole point: a precondition with no row is never driven,
which is how {SnapshotTrigger, orphan_pending} and handleSnapshot's reserve
race stayed unrecorded while both suites were green.
3. Every row whose code is a real error names its API handling in 'api' (below),
so a change in how the API treats an emission is a change to THIS file.
4. Adding a precondition is two edits -- an entry in 'preconditions' and a
fixture in the Worker test's driveRow -- after which the matrix test
enumerates every cell that now needs a decision.
The two tests enforce the two directions:
- worker: worker/internal/application/instancemanager/contract_test.go.
TestContractTableIsExhaustive checks the TABLE against the matrix (a cell with
no row is red) and TestContractTableCoversEveryHandledKind against Handle's
switch; TestCommandErrorContract drives the instancemanager into every
non-'unaffected' row's precondition and asserts the emitted code equals 'code'.
- api: api/tests/servers/test_command_error_contract.py DERIVES its expectations
from the 'api' column: the (module, function, CommandStatus) triples declared
across the rows must equal the triples its ast scan finds in
api/src/mc_server_dashboard_api/servers/application/. So a new API match on a
(kind, code) the Worker never emits has no row to live on (the #202 incident),
a declared site deleted from the source is red, and there is no hand-maintained
count anybody can nudge.
The 'api' column values:
[ "module.py:qualname", ... ] - the pair is MATCHED at these sites, and the list
must name ALL of them. An entry prefixed 'via ' is a consumer
of a discriminator declared on the same row (it holds no
CommandStatus reference of its own, so the Python scan does
not see it) -- e.g. the periodic snapshot scheduler reading
is_working_set_absent_refusal.
"command_failed"   - no match site: the outcome falls through to the API's
generic dispatch failure and its command_failed reason.
"fire_and_forget"  - the API awaits no result for this kind (RELAY.md Section 4,
BEDROCK_TUNNEL.md), so the refusal reaches only the
diagnostic log in fleet/adapters/control_plane.py.
omitted            - nothing to handle: the row is a success or 'unaffected'.
The port_conflict / image_missing rows are sanitized categories the container
driver derives from the Docker daemon's free-text error message (substring
detection -- see classifyStartError); the Worker test drives a fake driver
returning the wrapped sentinel rather than a live daemon. They are pinned so the
API may match them for a friendlier 409 reason (issue #225).
This table pins the deterministic per-kind precondition codes only; the
environment-dependent 'internal' and 'transfer_failed' codes are intentionally
left unpinned -- no row carries them, and a handler answering one is reporting a
failed operation, not a precondition.

preconditions.name: instance_running
description: a tracked running instance exists for the server id

preconditions.name: running_working_set_absent
description: a tracked running instance exists but the id's working-set claim -- the
generation marker at the scratch root -- is gone: the scratch was destroyed or
emptied out of band UNDER the live process (issue #2802). The relaunch of a
RestartServer is the only launch that can meet it, because every other
reserve()-gated kind is decided by the running instance before it reaches the
working set

preconditions.name: instance_stopped
description: no tracked instance, orphan or reservation for the id, and the id's working
set IS present at the scratch root (a prior hydrate/run left it): the state a
stopped-id SnapshotTrigger packs

preconditions.name: working_set_absent
description: no tracked instance, orphan or reservation, and the id's working dir does NOT
exist at the scratch root: already GC'd after a published final snapshot (a
benign duplicate SnapshotTrigger re-dispatched over a dropped stream), or never
hydrated on this Worker (issue #1713). It is the same Worker state a running-
server verb meets for an id this Worker knows nothing about, so it carries that
meaning too -- the former 'instance_absent' named this exact state under a
second name and was retired with the matrix (issue #2472)

preconditions.name: working_set_emptied
description: no tracked instance, orphan or reservation; the id's dir EXISTS at the scratch
root but holds no generation marker -- the contents were destroyed in place, or
only a crashed 204 stamp's '.mcsd_generation-*' temp survives (issue #2802). The
#2499 guard was a directory stat, which this shape passed; the marker predicate
refuses it exactly as it refuses working_set_absent

preconditions.name: command_in_flight
description: a mutating lifecycle command is reserved in flight for the id but no
instance/orphan is tracked yet (issue #780): a detached stop still confirming
termination, or a start/hydrate mid driver.Start / transfer after a stream
reconnect. The Worker emits 'busy' (issue #824) from the gates that consult the
reservation, distinct from the settled-state 'invalid_state', so the API retries
on a later tick rather than converging an observed state on the race

preconditions.name: orphan_pending
description: a failed-stop orphan is recorded (issue #251/#253): an instance whose driver
Stop could not confirm termination. Since issue #2475 this is never a settled
state -- a per-orphan converger probes the process, retries the stop while it is
alive, and retires the record once it is confirmed gone -- so the code splits by
whether the refused command WILL succeed after that (issue #2476):
'busy' for the reserve()-gated kinds (StartServer, HydrateTrigger, stopped-id
SnapshotTrigger), which the API retries until the convergence lets them
through. Answering 'invalid_state' there was the #2467 wedge: the API reads an
INVALID_STATE start as 'already running' and converged observed=running off a
refusal that may equally mean the process is already DEAD.
'invalid_state' for RestartServer / ServerCommand / TunnelDial /
OpenBedrockTunnel, which are refused for what the state IS and will never be
executed later, so 'busy' -- a promise of eventual success -- would be
dishonest.
The asymmetry is deliberate; do not unify it for symmetry. Two kinds are exempt
from any refusal and their rows pin that: StopServer TAKES the orphan and
re-attempts the driver Stop (the path that resolves it), and CloseBedrockTunnel
takes no running check at all, so the tunnel a failed stop left open (issue
#2468) can still be torn down (issue #2470 checked this rather than assuming it)

preconditions.name: snapshot_reserve_race
description: an instance is registered between handleSnapshot's UNRESERVED running check and
the stopped path's reserve(), so that reserve() finds a running instance and
answers 'server already running'. Only handleSnapshot reads the running flag
outside a reservation, so the window exists for no other kind. Recorded rather
than fixed (issue #2472, found by the #2495 review): the Worker test enters the
window through the manager's snapshotAfterRunningCheck seam, so the row is
DRIVEN by the real interleaving instead of asserted by prose

preconditions.name: driver_unavailable
description: the driver this command must use is not offered by this Worker. Only handleStart
and handleRestart resolve one from m.drivers: a start takes it from the command,
a restart from the RECORDED start spec of the instance it evicts (issue #1619)

preconditions.name: port_conflict
description: the driver Start failed on a host-port collision (#225). A RestartServer's
relaunch reaches it too, not only a StartServer

preconditions.name: image_missing
description: the driver Start failed on a missing container image (#225). A RestartServer's
relaunch reaches it too, not only a StartServer

preconditions.name: missing_path
description: the file/dir target does not exist in the working set

preconditions.name: unsafe_path
description: a traversal-rejected path (FR-FILE-4)

preconditions.name: unsafe_server_id
description: a server id rejected at command intake before any scratch-path join: empty,
'.'/'..', or one bearing a path separator / NUL (issue #782). The guard fires in
Manager.Handle ahead of the kind switch, so it applies identically to every kind
-- and every kind now carries the row saying so

rows.why: reserve()'s running refusal precedes launchReserved's working-set guard, so a start over a running instance is decided before it ever looks at the scratch: the {StartServer, instance_running} row is this cell's answer

the API issues a HydrateTrigger before every StartServer that needs one (control_plane.proto, StartServer), so a working set this Worker cannot show AT LAUNCH means a hydrate was skipped over one it does not actually hold. Starting anyway boots the server into an empty directory -- the #696 class, and the one residual of the held-inventory design that fails toward a SKIPPED hydrate rather than an extra one (issue #2499). Since issue #2802 the guard lives in launchReserved (so the restart's relaunch takes it too) and its predicate is the GENERATION MARKER, not a directory stat: an absent dir fails it because the marker's path resolves to nothing, and the emptied-in-place shape is the sibling working_set_emptied row. The refusal is what makes the API re-launch with a full hydrate; it does not break a first start, because a 204 hydrate still stamps the marker (writeGenerationGuarded)

the guard's predicate is the GENERATION MARKER (exact name .mcsd_generation; '.mcsd_generation-*' temps do not count), not a directory stat (issue #2802): the marker is the Worker's held-claim token -- a 200 hydrate embeds it atomically before the swap-in (issue #917), a 204 stamps it (writeGenerationGuarded), and the Worker declares a held generation only when the stamp landed (issue #2500) -- so a dir emptied in place has lost the claim the skipped hydrate relied on and refuses exactly like an absent one, same phrase, same API replay. A marker-ONLY dir (the 204 nothing-published case) PASSES: the fresh-start boot is the 204 contract, which is why a content predicate ('level.dat present') would be wrong. Residual: a destruction that spares the marker but eats content still boots

the running path takes no reservation: it brackets the pack with the save-off/save-all quiesce instead (issue #829 item 4)

DRIVEN, and not what issue #2802 predicted (transfer_failed via the quiesce): the running path takes no working-set check by design -- it is reservation-free and the save-off/save-all bracket is its quiesce (issue #829 item 4) -- and both collaborators treat an absent root as empty rather than as an error, by explicit contract: scanRegionState yields an empty settled map, and packTar 'snapshots an empty/absent working dir to an empty tar'. So the Worker packs and offers nothing and answers ok. The production backstop is API-side: the upload stages zero files and is refused 400 empty_snapshot (dataplane/api/transfers.py) before any generation publishes, which reaches the Worker as the environment-dependent transfer_failed this table leaves unpinned -- a failed operation, not a precondition code. Recorded per the #202 discipline: the code is what driveRow shows, never the prediction

the stopped-id guard's predicate is the working set's CONTENT -- hasWorkingSet: at least one child that is not the generation marker or one of its '.mcsd_generation-*' temps -- not a directory stat (issue #2813). An emptied dir passed the stat, so the Worker packed nothing: the pack excludes the marker and its temps, the upload stages zero files, and the API refuses it 400 empty_snapshot (dataplane/api/transfers.py, storage/adapters/fs.py) only AFTER a full pack+upload -- the wasted cycle #1713 closed for the absent dir, repeated every scheduler tick, and reported as the environment-dependent transfer_failed, which points away from the cause. It is refused at the source instead, with the code and the pinned 'working dir absent' phrase the periodic scheduler already reads as 'nothing left to capture' (issue #2480). The predicate deliberately DIFFERS from the launch guard's on this same precondition: a marker-ONLY dir PASSES the launch guard (the 204 fresh-boot contract) but is refused here, because there is nothing for the pack to stage; content WITHOUT a marker packs, which is correct -- there is a world to capture
